content:
GRACE Follow-On tracks changes in Earth’s water by measuring the changing distance between two satellites.

The pair follows one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart. As they pass a larger concentration of mass, gravity affects the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther ahead and increasing the gap between them.

That change in separation helps scientists infer shifts in mass. Those shifts can reveal changes in groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers and ice sheets, and sea level when water is added to the oceans.

A changing distance between two satellites becomes a way to investigate how water is moving across Earth.
